ios.desc:
Notevision is your essential tool for mastering sight reading and building real musical skill. Whether you’re just starting out or refining advanced technique, Notevision helps you learn faster and play with confidence.

Why Musicians Choose Notevision:

Interactive Sight-Reading Exercises
	•	Targeted practice sessions that quickly sharpen accuracy, rhythm, and note recognition.

Flexible Practice Options
	•	Use a MIDI instrument, your device’s microphone, or the built-in on-screen keyboard.

Adaptive Difficulty
	•	Adjust challenge levels to match your skill and grow at your own pace.

Music Theory Made Simple
	•	Learn key signatures, accidentals, and rhythms—and explore the new key signature reference for quick lookups.

Interactive Chord Reference
	•	Browse essential chords with clear visuals and playback support.

Chord Practice Mode
	•	Reinforce chord recognition and harmonic understanding through guided exercises.

Progress Tracking
	•	Gain motivation from detailed insights that show your improvement over time.

Songs & Randomized Practice
	•	Combine structured lessons with curated songs and endlessly varied note patterns.

Begin your musical journey with Notevision—learn smarter, play better, and build confidence every day.

show_hn.title: Show HN: My iOS app to practice sight reading (10 years in the App Store)

quotes.text:
Hello HN, this has been my personal project for quite some time now. It has been a slowly evolving project over the years and its core function is for users to expose themselves to progressively more difficult lessons of music notes.

NOTE: It is free and there are no ads. There is an in app purchase but most of the app doesn't require it.

quotes.text: This is an excellent article and I can relate. I'm in my early 30's and I took up piano a year and a half ago. Learning music has been a great outlet and gives me something to study that has nothing to do with programming. I've taken lessons the entire time and I've found the best help my instructor has given me was telling me what I was doing wrong that I'd never be able to see. It's fun to learn something new and I feel music is a mystery that was similar to when I started down the engineering path. Even though its an escape I still ended up making an iOS app to practice sight reading since I didn't like what was out there. It's a shameless plug but its available and is free with no ads or iaps: https://itunes.apple.com/us/app/music-note-sight-reading-trainer/id874386416?mt=8
